source.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: Curse of Dimensionality and Structural Bias
source.authors: Yun-Hao Ni; Yu-Xin Guo; Jie Luo; Wen-Jun Wu; Lei Huang

page_placements.theme: Practical memorization and its generalization cost depend on model and procedure

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests random-label fitting on MNIST using a parameter-budget scan and reports training accuracy, a different setting and measure from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The random-label experiment reports MNIST training accuracy by model family and parameter budget. It does not report random-label test error or compare random-label training time with true-label training time. Other versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study measures random-label training accuracy directly, extending the fitting test to MNIST architecture and parameter-budget scans. It uses the same basic measure as the original, rather than a different measure as the record suggests.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the random-label experiment: within the prescribed architecture and optimizer scan, ReLU-MLPs fit randomized MNIST labels more efficiently in parameter count than spline-only KANs. This does not establish faster convergence time.
record.recipe_differences: Uses randomized MNIST labels and reports final training accuracy across architecture and parameter-budget scans; the original claim's settings are not reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: MNIST parameter budget and model family; random-label fitting improves with larger ReLU-MLP budgets, while spline-only KAN accuracy remains below 20% in the reported budget table.

fits_no_version.finding: Spline-only KAN random-label training accuracy remains between 12.3% and 19.4% at the four reported budgets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under this scan and training protocol, spline-only KANs fit random MNIST labels substantially less effectively than ReLU-MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: Both model families improve standard-label test accuracy as the parameter budget increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested models can generalize on normally labeled MNIST, with ReLU-MLPs attaining higher test accuracy within these budgets.

record.problems: The experiment is limited to MNIST and the scanned model families and budgets. It reports random-label training accuracy, not random-label test error. Optimizer and learning rate are selected by final training accuracy; the paper does not establish unchanged hyperparameters between label conditions. The table reports medians over three seeds but gives no uncertainty values there.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table 1 reports all four parameter budgets for both model families under standard and random labels; all 16 rows are included.

untested.parts: Random-label test error at chance and successful fitting with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters relative to true labels. The architecture grids are shared, but architectures and optimizer/rate combinations are selected within conditions.
Relative convergence time for true versus random labels and convergence as corruption fraction increases; a fixed 200-epoch protocol does not measure these.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Intermediate label-corruption fractions, perfect training fit across fractions, and the corresponding test-error trajectory.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation. No regularization comparison is reported.
Learning real patterns before noisy labels and differences in learning dynamics; only final random-label training accuracy is reported.

missing.what: Random-label results for the fixed 6,000-image subset: the MLP eventually fits every training label. Extract the available model/budget conditions from Figure 14.

Architecture-specific random-label accuracies distinguish width and depth effects hidden by the budget envelope. For example, width-256 MLPs report 99%, 100%, 97%, and 96% at hidden depths 2, 4, 6, and 8 respectively.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 values and aggregation match the supplied text. They are selected architecture medians over three seeds, not individual-run guarantees. The nominal random-label chance accuracy is 10%; no significance tests justify treating small above-chance values as absent. The record also incorrectly marks code availability as unstated: the paper says experiment code and compact result tables are available in a GitHub repository.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label test error at chance; whether fitting uses the same architecture and training hyperparameters as the true-label condition; near-zero training error at budgets other than those reported.
